# Issues

**The register of everything open in this repo.** Defects, gaps, and questions
awaiting a ruling. One id per item, stable forever.

**This file is the source of truth for what is open.** Nothing is open unless it
is here. Other documents no longer carry their own open-item lists — they link
here. Long analysis may stay where it was argued (`packages/*/PROJECT_STATE.md`,
`IDEAS/*.md`); the **Detail** column points at it. What must
never happen again is an item existing in exactly one document that nobody reads.

**What belongs here:** shipped behavior that is wrong, a gap that blocks
something, a question that needs a decision. **What does not:** features and
roadmap (`IDEAS/`), settled rulings (`DECISIONS.md`), traps that are correct
behavior you must know about (`CLAUDE.md` § Live hazards), history
(git, `FJS-D675`).

**Closed items age out to [ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md).**
§ Closed below keeps the recent ones; the archive keeps the rest, verbatim.
Together they hold every id ever issued, and an id is never reused — so a
`FJS-###` named in a comment, a handoff, or a package file resolves in exactly
one of the two files. Search both before concluding an id is unknown.

## Conventions

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Id** | `FJS-###` for a defect or gap, `FJS-D##` for a decision. **Never reused, never renumbered.** Closing an item moves it to § Closed with its id. |
| **Sev** | `S1` blocker — data loss, a security hole, or cannot ship · `S2` high — silently wrong, costs a day to find · `S3` medium · `S4` low or cosmetic |
| **Status** | `open` — verified open on the date shown · `stale?` — inherited from an older audit and **not re-verified**; probe before acting · `contested` — the recorded diagnosis is doubted, see the note |
| **Verified** | The date somebody last ran it. A `stale?` row's date is when it was *written*, not confirmed. |
| **Blocked by** | A row that cannot start until another closes says `blocked by FJS-###` in its own text, and nowhere else. `fli next` takes it out of the ranking until that row closes and weighs the blocker up. Write it only where the order is real — a row that merely relates to another cites it. |
| **By hand** | A row a headless session cannot finish — a run longer than a session lasts, a check only the owner can make — says `by hand` as its own segment of its links cell. `fli next` keeps it ranked and marks it; `fix:loop` skips it. |
| **Env** | A row whose fix is the environment and not the code says `env: <cause>` as its own segment of its links cell, cause one of `port` · `shared db` · `stale process` · `timing` · `real machine` · `network` (`FJS-D1118`). The segment names where the FIX lives, not where the symptom shows. `fli next` keeps it ranked and marks it; `fix:loop` skips it; `fli register:check` refuses a cause outside the list (`env-cause`) and warns on a title that reads like one with no segment (`env-smell`). |
| **Seam** | A row whose bug crosses a named handoff says `seam: <name>` as its own segment of its links cell, the name from the root `CLAUDE.md` § Bridge index key list (`FJS-D1135`). `env:` names where the fix lives; `seam:` names which handoff the bug crosses. Written by hand; `fli register:check` refuses a name the key list does not hold (`seam-name`). |

**A row has exactly the columns its table's header names**, and `fli
register:check` fails on anything else (`row-shape`). Both ways of getting it
wrong are silent: a row with FEWER columns is one pasted from the other table,
and the reader infers a shape from the cell count, so it is given a status
nobody wrote and no other rule can see it; a row with MORE has the excess
**dropped when the file is rendered** — in § Closed that is the *How* column, so
the row displays with no citations while they sit in the file. Links belong
inside the last declared column, joined with ` · `, and a `|` that is part of a
sentence is escaped `\|`.

`stale?` is load-bearing. The eight rows inherited from the 2026-07-31 audit
(now `IDEAS/review-coherence.md`) were re-probed on 2026-08-10 and **five of the eight were wrong**:
two were already fixed (conduit's secrets, `admin:generate`), one was never
reproducible (conduit's version skew), and two were right about a defect and
wrong about what it was — sierra's prefetch is not an auth *bypass* but a
cached 401, and caravan's row named three bugs of which two were fixed.
**Treat a `stale?` row as a lead, not a fact** (`VERIFYING.md`).

**The register also goes stale in the closing direction, which nothing here was
watching for.** `FJS-043` was fixed in the tree with a comment describing the
old defect in the past tense, and stayed `open` for eight days because closing
is a second action nobody owed. A row's `Verified` date is evidence about when
somebody last *looked*, not about whether the defect survives — 22 rows carried
`open` at 2026-08-02 when this audit ran, which is the same fiction `stale?`
exists to name, wearing the other label.

| Id | Pkg | Title | Status | Verified | Detail |

| <a id="fjs-4005"></a>FJS-4005 | litestone | **One many-write on a model with an @big column poisons SELECT changes() for the life of the process — every later deleteMany on a plain model throws TypeError: Invalid mix of BigInt and other type in addition, a 500 to the caller** | open | 2026-11-04 | Measured 2026-11-04, immich Phase 5 (immich-94): the album page's Remove from album answered 500 on the dev server from the first Empty trash onward, 200 on a fresh process; minimal sequence is assetFile.deleteMany (size Int @big) then albumAsset.deleteMany, both zero rows, on a VACUUM INTO copy. Cause: rowsChanged() reads the count with db.query('SELECT changes() AS n') (core/databases.js), the wide model's wideDb.query wraps the CACHED statement in wideStmt, which calls stmt.safeIntegers(true) on it — the cache entry every model shares for that SQL. The wide model narrows its own read, the next plain model gets n = 0n and the write loop's count += n (core/client.js) throws. updateMany is spared (RETURNING). Fix shape: a changes() statement of its own, or safeIntegers on a clone rather than the cache entry · [bigint-changes-probe.mjs](../fjs-prototypes/immich/measure/bigint-changes-probe.mjs) · [databases.js](packages/litestone/src/core/databases.js) · [client.js](packages/litestone/src/core/client.js) · [PLAN.md](../fjs-prototypes/immich/PLAN.md) · FJS-D174 (safeIntegers is per statement) |
| <a id="fjs-4002"></a>FJS-4002 | cli | **A workspace command run outside a workspace with no TTY on stdin never exits and spins a core: context.wsRoot's readline prompt waits on stdin at EOF forever** | open | 2026-11-04 | Measured 2026-11-04: from fjs-prototypes/immich (not a workspace, no WORKSPACE_DIR), 'fli sig setCallDb </dev/null' prints the 'Workspace root path' prompt and sits at 100% of a core until killed; an agent's call left one running 10h45m, 10h23m of CPU. Every agent shell's stdin is /dev/null, so any $.wsRoot() command (fli sig and others) hangs this way outside the workspace. Fix: prompt only when process.stdin.isTTY, resolve null on rl 'close', and say how to set WORKSPACE_DIR · [cli core/runtime.js](packages/cli/core/runtime.js) · [sig.md](packages/cli/commands/utils/sig.md) |
| <a id="fjs-4001"></a>FJS-4001 | sierra | **Sierra's dev schema watcher watches the whole of db/, so Vite holds a watch on every stored media file and every WAL write, and pegs a core while an app writes there** | open | 2026-11-04 | Measured in fjs-prototypes/immich (2026-11-04): during a 10k-asset thumbnail derive, vite dev held ~28k inotify watches, 99% of a 300-sample under db/storage, and used ~90% of a core for 25 min (22 min CPU) with RSS ~1 GB. Cause: the FJS-1470 fix calls server.watcher.add(dirname(schemaPath)), which is recursive and reaches db/storage, db/uploads and the *.db-wal files. Only schema.lite is wanted: watch with depth 0, or ignore every path but the schema. App-side workaround: server.watch.ignored in web/config/vite.config.js · [sierra build/schema-plugin.js](packages/sierra/src/build/schema-plugin.js) · [FJS-1470](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1470) |

| <a id="fjs-3998"></a>FJS-3998 | junction | **bearerClaim.redeem() has no seam for a second factor, so a share link with a password is redeemed by an app route that matches the @hashed password in a where and then calls the handler** | open | 2026-11-04 | immich 4.2 (Q6), 2026-11-04. redeem(db, opts) reads only { token } from the body, finds the row by the token's digest and sets the cookie; nothing in it can refuse on the row's other columns. The album link with a password (Share.passwordHash @hashed, @@trait(Grant)) needed: POST /shares/{id}/redeem as a route file, body { token, password }, sys.share.findFirst({ where: { id, passwordHash: password ?? null } }) first — a row with no password matches null, one with a password matches its own — then redeem(ctx). It works (share.test.ts: no password 401, wrong 401, right 200 + cookie, again 401, one sentence for all four) but the id has to travel in the URL because the app cannot find the row by the token (it does not hold the resolver's digest), and the password check and the token check are two lookups two layers apart. A redeem option such as verify(row, body) → boolean, or where: (body) => ({ passwordHash: body.password ?? null }), would keep both in the one lookup and let the URL carry the token alone. · api/src/routes/shares/[id]/redeem.ts · api/test/share.test.ts · SECOND SIGHTING 2026-11-04 (immich 5.2, the share page): because every refusal is the same 401 (FJS-D696), the page cannot learn that a link asks for a password until a redeem without one has failed — share/[id].mesa redeems bare first and shows the password field on the 401, which is the only shape the seam allows; a redeem that could say "password needed" would let the page ask first |
| <a id="fjs-3996"></a>FJS-3996 | junction | **A @@commitment hook writing a gate-8 model through ctx.db is refused: the fire's client is the app's system principal (SYSADMIN), the fire fails and retries with the error only in the queue row, and the working spelling, ctx.db.asSystem() inside the fire's transaction, is documented nowhere** | open | 2026-11-04 | Met building immich PLAN.md step 4.1 (Q5): the Asset.purge hook (api/src/domain/assets/asset.commitments.ts) frees a purged asset's derived files with ctx.db.assetFile.deleteMany — AssetFile is @@gate(0.8.8.8), the pipeline's rows. The fire failed '"AssetFile.delete" requires SYSTEM access (use asSystem())', went pending with attempts 1 and a later run_at, and the app log said nothing at any level: the error sat in jobs.db's row (error column) and the test saw only a row still trashed after 15 s. FJS-D368 says the hook runs 'on the fire's client', which is createApp({ system }) — the app's own principal, graded by its gate (SYSADMIN here), never 8. The spelling that works: ctx.db.asSystem().assetFile.deleteMany inside the hook; $transaction hands the hook the client proxy on the exclusive connection, so the system copy taken inside stays in the move's transaction (the test's rows and objects go with the commit). Owed: (1) a fire's failure printed to the log, not only the queue row — a hook that throws is otherwise a row that never moves and a job retrying quietly; (2) the hook context says which standing ctx.db has and that asSystem() on it is the way to a gate-8 child, or hands a system client beside it · [tombstone.test.ts](../fjs-prototypes/immich/api/test/tombstone.test.ts) · [asset.commitments.ts](../fjs-prototypes/immich/api/src/domain/assets/asset.commitments.ts) · [FJS-D368](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d368) |

Proved with a probe app: a real device key in Authorization: Bearer on PUT /api/probe/stream and PUT /api/probe/plain — both handlers saw ctx.user null and ctx.locals undefined, and both answered 200, so a dead or revoked key passes a raw route in silence. Calling the resolver by hand with the raw ctx throws 'no accessor device on the client' (no callDb, no locals); the workaround that works is setCallDb({ headers: ctx.headers, user: null, locals: {} }, db) then await deviceBearer(fake, null), which yields the claims and locals['bearer:device'] and throws 401 for a dead key — then the route still has to scope its own client (db.$setAuth(claims)). | <a id="fjs-3731"></a>FJS-3731 | junction | **A move invoked by name runs no patch hook and takes no ctx.data, so the columns a before-patch hook stamps (who moved) stay null** | open | 2026-10-31 | expenses stressor. Claim.submit/approve/approveFirst/bounce called as service.invoke(name, id) (the door a sierra page uses for a machine move) never reach hooks.before.patch, and a before hook on the move has no ctx.data to write: submittedById/approvedBy1Id stayed null, so the four-eyes row policies (FJS-3692/3693) compare against null and a submitter could approve. Worked around with hooks.after on each move writing the columns as asSystem (api/src/core/movers.ts), which also leaves lastMovedById to the system write. Evidence: measure/screens.mjs rows 19/25 before the after hooks. Option B of FJS-3694 (engine-written WHO) removes the hook; until then every door to a move needs the stamp. Related: FJS-3693, FJS-3694. · blocked by `FJS-D1706` |
| <a id="fjs-3725"></a>FJS-3725 | junction | **A filter cannot name the caller: the approver inbox needs the client to bring its own Employee id, and nothing in the session carries it** | open | 2026-10-31 | expenses stressor Q5 (measure/inbox.mjs). The inbox (submitted and not mine, or approved1 by someone else) IS sayable as a ctx.query — $or[0][status]=submitted&$or[0][submittedById][not]=<id>&$or[1][status]=approved1&$or[1][approvedBy1Id][not]=<id> — but only with the caller literal: the operator ne is refused (Unknown where operator ne ... one of: ... not, notIn ...), and no token (auth().employeeId, @me) exists in a filter. The login user carries no employeeId (claim employeeId from Employee(userId) is graded server-side and never projected), so a screen reads its own Employee row first. The filter is advisory: a manager can read every claim, so the inbox is a UI affordance and the policies, not the filter, refuse the wrong approver (Invariant 6 holds). Ask: a caller token in a where, or a documented sessionFields projection of declared claims. · blocked by `FJS-D1730` |
| <a id="fjs-3723"></a>FJS-3723 | litestone | **Copy paths that carry a tenant's bytes outside its placement: backup (one backups/ root, --zip), replicate, export --out, studio, with no per-tenant exclude** | open | 2026-10-31 | clinical stressor Q5 (measure/residency.mjs). Under strategy database 'litestone backup' copies tenant-files (every <id>.db in the one tenancy dir) plus tenant-registry into backups/<stamp>/ beside the schema: one destination for the whole fleet, no flag to leave one tenant out (flags are dest, --db, --vacuum, --zip); an EU clinic's file inside that dir is carried to the default backup root and --zip makes it one portable archive. 'litestone replicate' streams every sqlite file to the one configured S3/R2 target, tenant files included (cli.js tenantStorage pattern '*.db'). 'litestone export <dataset> --out <dir>' writes ndjson to any directory and --stdout to a pipe; the --tenant flag picks the tenant but nothing checks where the bytes go. 'litestone studio' (loopback by default, --host + --token beyond) opens any tenant file and browses/edits its rows in a browser; its Tenants panel lists the registry. None reads a residency declaration because none exists (FJS-3722). Acceptance: a tenant marked resident is skipped by backup/replicate unless the destination is declared for it, and export/studio name it in their output. Row-strategy (clinical) is the worse case: one app.db carries both clinics, so backup of 'the EU clinic' is not expressible at all. · blocked by `FJS-D1743` |

| <a id="fjs-3715"></a>FJS-3715 | litestone | **Correcting a @personal column keeps no original anywhere: the trail's before and after are both [personal]** | open | 2026-10-31 | clinical stressor (measure/proxy.mjs, PLAN Q3/Q4), 2026-10-30. Patient.dateOfBirth DateTime @personal(demographic), @@trail(audit, reads: true). Admin PATCH /api/patients/:id {dateOfBirth} -> 200; the update entry reads before {dateOfBirth: '[personal]'} after {dateOfBirth: '[personal]'} (Invariant 7, as designed). So the original value survives nowhere -- not the live row, not the trail. A clinical record's rule is 'the original never changes; a correction is appended' (PLAN Q3), which @seals/@immutable give a Note but no word gives a person's own column without making it immutable outright. | <a id="fjs-3710"></a>FJS-3710 | conduit | **A write a conduit Receiver's apply makes files in the trail as actorType system with actorId, source and meta all null: the trail cannot tell a card-network webhook's Charge from any other asSystem() write, nor name the provider or the delivery** | open | 2026-10-31 | Found by the expenses stressor 1.4 (fjs-prototypes/expenses/measure/charge-order.mjs row 'webhook create, actor columns'). | <a id="fjs-3708"></a>FJS-3708 | litestone | **A read the row policy refuses leaves no trail entry, under @@trail(audit, reads: true)** | open | 2026-10-31 | clinical stressor (measure/glass.mjs, PLAN Q1/Q2), 2026-10-30. Same for a list whose where matches nothing (measure/read-trail.mjs wherePersonalNoHit: 0 rows). A regulated read log records who OPENED a chart and not who TRIED to: an attempted open of a chart outside the care team is the event a privacy officer most needs (PLAN Q6), and the 404 also hides from the caller that a door exists (FJS-3696). Whether an attempt row may carry the id it named is an Invariant 7 question the fix has to answer. · Refused WRITES leave none either (clinical measure/addenda.mjs, 2026-10-30). On a signed Note: PATCH body -> 409 sealed, trail +0; PATCH status draft -> 409, +0; PATCH a LOCKED Addendum -> 403, +0; DELETE -> 403 @@require message, +1 row 'read Note user' (the require's WHERE), no delete-attempt row. Under asSystem(): note.update body throws SealedDocumentError, +0; note.delete / deleteMany answer null / {count: 0} with NO throw and +0 -- @@require held, silently. So neither a refused clinician nor a job that tried to delete a signed note leaves evidence. · blocked by `FJS-D1707` · blocked by `FJS-D1707` |
| <a id="fjs-3694"></a>FJS-3694 | litestone | **A row policy cannot read the row's own history: 'nobody approves what they themselves last moved' needs the audit trail, which no policy expression reaches -- ruling candidate: may a move's gate quantify over the row's history?** | open | 2026-10-31 | Found by the expenses stressor 0.3 (fjs-prototypes/expenses/discovery/open-questions.md § Cannot say D). Tried: @@deny(update, $trail.last.actorId == auth().id) -- refused 'Expected a value in policy expression, got $'. The trail is in audit.db, a separate database, so a SQL-compiled policy has no join to it. The easy version (lastMovedById String? @updatedBy) compiles but records the last WRITER, not the last MOVER: any non-move edit overwrites it. Phase 1.3 measures both. · Measured, expenses 1.3: the trail already holds what rule 3 needs -- each Claim move files transition ('submit', 'approveFirst', 'approve', 'pay') and the user's actorId; only a policy cannot reach it (audit.db is another database). The easy version, @@deny(update, (status == 'submitted' \|\| status == 'approved1') && lastMovedById == auth().id) with lastMovedById @updatedBy, holds over HTTP and WS but grades the last WRITER: the submitter can no longer edit their own submitted claim. Options A/B/C in fjs-prototypes/expenses/PLAN.md § Q1. · Ruled FJS-D1699 (2026-10-31): B, as recommended — @stamps gains by: <principal column> and an engine-kept last-mover column; closes FJS-3693 with the build. · blocked by `FJS-D1731` |
| <a id="fjs-3692"></a>FJS-3692 | litestone | **A @@transitions move cannot be keyed to a predicate on the actor: @gate takes only a level and a policy names no move, so four-eyes (approver != submittedById) is a @@deny(update) that also forbids the submitter's every other write** | open | 2026-10-31 | Found by the expenses stressor 0.3 (fjs-prototypes/expenses/discovery/open-questions.md § Cannot say A, C). Tried: approve: [submitted, approved1] -> approved @gate(auth().employeeId != submittedById) -- refused '@gate expects a level 0-9, got auth'; @@deny(approve, submittedById == auth().employeeId) -- refused 'invalid operation approve. Valid: read, create, update, postUpdate, delete, write, all'. What compiles is @@deny(update, status == 'submitted' && submittedById == auth().employeeId), which is not move-keyed: it also refuses a withdrawal or any edit by the submitter while submitted, so the schema says the rule wider than the business does, or twice (row policy + app check). Related: FJS-D1025 (role-limited move). Phase 1.1 measures it over HTTP, WS and asSystem(). · Measured, expenses 1.1 (fjs-prototypes/expenses/measure/four-eyes.mjs): @@deny(postUpdate, (status == 'approved1' \|\| status == 'approved') && submittedById == auth().employeeId) keys rule 1 to the TARGET state and holds over HTTP and WS -- closer than the pre-image @@deny(update), though still not the move. The refusal names the move ('"Claim.approve" was refused by an @@allow/@@deny policy') which no policy can. Second sighting of the shape: the threshold choice (submitted -> approved only below Company.approvalThresholdCents) has no spelling on the move and lives in the same hook, a BadRequest. · blocked by `FJS-D1025` |

Publishing a static App there failed with *path 'assets/_...404_-U15rT7nd.js' has a segment that is not a plain file name* — Vite's chunk for a `[...404]` route — which 0.1.5 refuses and [static.js](packages/outpost/src/static.js) has allowed since 7ae59353 (2026-10-23). The way forward was `sed` over the unit, `daemon-reload`, restart. Basecamp records `outpostVersion` off each heartbeat and knows the version it installs (`OUTPOST_VERSION`, [enrollment.ts](packages/basecamp/api/src/providers/compute/enrollment.ts)), so it can see the gap and offer nothing. Fix candidates: a Server action (and `fli` command) that rewrites the pin and restarts through `/exec` or ssh, the certificate kept (`FJS-D557`); and `/servers/` marking a machine behind `OUTPOST_VERSION`. | <a id="fjs-3525"></a>FJS-3525 | cli | **basecamp:deploy preflight describes an App's first-release setup as prose fixes it could apply itself** | open | 2026-10-27 | Found running fli deploy --dry on ela (stressor 24) against a fresh App: 3 errors and 7 warnings, every one an App setting (port, health, volume + 5 DB paths, NODE_ENV, SA_URL, ENCRYPTION_KEY as a secret, Domain and the two FRONTIER_*_URLs). Proposal: (1) each finding carries its fix as data beside the hint — a Variables patch or an App patch — so the command can apply it; (2) a never-released App (no deployment, no port, no own Variables) is detected without a flag and opens a walkthrough: ask the Domain once, derive both URLs from it, generate ENCRYPTION_KEY unprinted, apply the mechanical patches, re-run the preflight; non-interactive prints the plan; (3) the same declared inputs (defineEnv, schema database blocks, health route, listen port) create the App right the first time, so the preflight becomes drift detection. Keep Dockerfile digest pins (a repo edit), a required credential and widgets/ out of auto-fix; the web/ static App IS created, with the Domain on it and the API's prefixes routed back (`FJS-D1547`, overriding this row's first draft). Built 2026-10-27: (1) and (2) in release-preflight.js + deploy.md; (3) is a second change once its shape is ruled · [deploy.md](packages/cli/commands/basecamp/deploy.md) · [release-preflight.js](packages/cli/core/release-preflight.js) · blocked by `FJS-D1652` |

| <a id="fjs-3125"></a>FJS-3125 | litestone | **A model with a @seals move has no word for 'frozen from CREATE', so an exam attempt's identity columns (userId, quizId, startedAt) stay rewritable by the sitter for the whole sitting — @immutable there means frozen at the seal** | open | 2026-10-16 | Measured by the moodle stressor (#10) Phase 2.1, measure/attempt-data.mjs § what a student can still rewrite on an OPEN attempt, createTestEnv over the real schema. Attempt declares userId/quizId/courseId/startedAt @immutable and a @seals move (submit); a student's own client then accepts update({ data: { quizId: <another quiz> } }), { startedAt: <yesterday> } and { userId: <another student> } on the open attempt (all three REWRITTEN, read back by asSystem). The row policy admits the write (userId == auth().id && status == 'inProgress'), the seal has not happened, and FJS-D167 priced exactly this: '@immutable changes meaning on a sealing model'. What it leaves is a draft whose ownership and quiz the sitter can move: quizId defeats the per-quiz maxAttempts count, userId hands a sitting to a classmate (or onto their unique slot). FJS-D568 added the LATER freeze (@immutable(after: move)); the EARLIER one has no spelling, and a row policy cannot compare old with new, so the app cannot write it either. Expected: a word (or an argument to @immutable) for 'frozen from create' that a sealing model can carry beside the seal-scoped one · [DECISIONS.md FJS-D167](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d167) · [FJS-D568](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d568) · [measure/attempt-data.mjs](../fjs-prototypes/moodle/measure/attempt-data.mjs) · blocked by `FJS-D1280` |
| <a id="fjs-3124"></a>FJS-3124 | junction · client | **A client subscription under a service's FILENAME spelling is deaf: `client.service('log-chunks').on('created')` receives nothing while `.find()` under the same name works, because FJS-D159's alias covers calls and an event is keyed by the name the client subscribed under** | open | 2026-10-16 | Found by the ci-runner stressor (Phase 2, a live log). `api/src/services/log-chunks.service.ts` derives the service `logChunks` (FJS-D159); `/api/log-chunks` and `/api/logChunks` both answer 200, and `client.service('log-chunks').find()` reads rows. The server publishes the frame as `logChunks created` (measured with a wrapped `app.channels.sendGraded`: `sendGraded ["log-chunks"] logChunks created {...}`), and the client listens for `${name} created` with the name it was handed. Measured on one run that wrote 56 chunks from a job: a listener on `service('log-chunks')` received 0 frames, a listener on `service('logChunks')` received all 56. No error anywhere; the page renders the stored rows once and then never moves, which is the stale-list symptom FJS-701 exists to make visible. The `channel:` string is a third spelling (`'log-chunks'`, the channel NAME a connection joins) and is unrelated, so three kebab/camel spellings of one service sit side by side and only one of them is live. A `.mesa` resource goes through Sierra's `serviceNameFor` (camelCase) and is fine, which is why nothing in the repo's own apps shows it; an app that writes `client.service` by hand against its file names is the one that does. Two answers: the client canonicalizes through the manifest's service names before it keys an event (the alias then covers subscriptions as D159 says it covers calls), or `service()` on an alias refuses a subscription by name. Workaround in the app: web/src/lib/follow-log.js names `logChunks`. · blocked by `FJS-D1342` |
| <a id="fjs-3123"></a>FJS-3123 | litestone · junction | **An update naming only @system columns is still charged the model's 'update' capability, so a commitment hook that stamps the move (expiredAt) is refused for the app principal, which holds no grants — every fire fails, retries and sits pending with the attempt still inProgress** | open | 2026-10-16 | Measured by the moodle stressor (#10) Phase 2.3 on Attempt (@@capabilities, @@commitment(expire, on: dueAt)). commitments({ hooks: { 'Attempt.expire': … } }) runs db.attempt.update({ where, data: { expiredAt }, system: ['expiredAt'] }) in the move's transaction as createApp({ system }); with the row visible to that principal (isSystemAdmin in the read and update @@allow, as ghost's FJS-2231 note says) the fire still fails every attempt: AccessDeniedError 'You do not hold the "Attempt.update" capability'. litestone plugins/capability.js _checkUpdate says a column named in system: [...] is not charged to the caller's grants, then charges 'update' anyway when no other key is graded (`ungraded.length \|\| (!graded.length && !moves.length)`): the same call as a principal holding Attempt.update succeeds (measured in-process, .fli-tmp/cap.mjs). The expire move itself is not charged (a @system move), so the clock moves the row and its own stamp is what a fire cannot write. Seven attempts stayed inProgress 150 s after the reboot with job rows commitment-fire pending, attempts 2 of 3, error as above, nothing on screen: the same quiet failure FJS-2231 named. Workaround in moodle: SYSTEM (api/src/core/gate.ts) carries capabilities: ['Attempt.update'], which makes the clock's principal hold a grant a person gave nobody · [capability.js](packages/litestone/src/plugins/capability.js) · [measure/attempt.mjs](../fjs-prototypes/moodle/measure/attempt.mjs) · [FJS-2801](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-2801) · blocked by `FJS-D1263` |

| <a id="fjs-3091"></a>FJS-3091 | junction | **Under strategy row, a custom method on a tenant-scoped service is refused when the request names no tenant, so a platform-wide operation over a scoped model (the weekly payout run) has no home on that model's service** | open | 2026-10-16 | etsy stressor (#11), Phase 1 (1.4). Payout carries shopId and is scoped by `tenancy { strategy row column shopId claim shopId }`. payouts.service.ts declared a custom method `run` — the weekly job's body: for EVERY shop with a payable balance, write a Payout through asSystem() and send one conduit transfer. An administrator's `POST /api/payouts` with `x-service-method: run` and no X-Shop-Id answers 400: 'This request names no shopId, and payouts is scoped to it by the schema — name one with the X-Shop-Id header.' The guard is right for CRUD, where every read is one tenant's, and wrong for a method whose definition is *across tenants* and reads nothing scoped through the caller. This is a ruling wearing a bug report: whether Caravan hands a handler a child-process helper (spawn in own group, kill group on abort, sweep on exit) or stays signal-only and documents that a handler that spawns owns its process group. | <a id="fjs-1246"></a>FJS-1246 | example | **`example`'s payroll has no input shape for a MEASURED hour: `annualGross` is `rate * hoursPerWeek * 52` and `hoursPerWeek` is an `Int` contracted constant, so a workforce product's whole output can reach a payslip only by being averaged back into the contract it was measured to replace.** | open | 2026-09-22 | **Graded, not ported** — PLAN.md § Q6 in the connectteam stressor, against the shapes `example/api/src/domain/payroll/` demands and with nothing copied into that tree. An approved timesheet (`@@transitions`, `@seals`, lines carrying `onDate`, `kind`, `minutes` and a `rateSnapshot` frozen at the rate in force on the day) was converted into `PayWindowRow` and run through transcribed copies of `annualGross` and `periodShare`. **It goes, and everything that makes it a measurement is lost on the way.** Spring fortnight: 420 measured minutes, **€84.00 actually earned**, → `{ basis: 'hourly', rate: 1200, hoursPerWeek: 4 }` → `annualGross` €2496.00 → `periodShare(·, 26)` **€96.00 — out by €12.00**. Autumn fortnight: 540 minutes, €108.00 earned → `hoursPerWeek: 5` → €3120.00 → **€120.00, out by €12.00**. **Four refusals, and only the fourth is one a type checker catches.** (1) `hoursPerWeek` is an `Int @gte(0) @lte(168)`, so a fortnight holding one 7-hour night is **3.5 h/week and is stored as 4** — the rounding alone is the whole €12.00. (2) `PayWindow` holds ONE `rate` for a window while a timesheet holds a `rateSnapshot` per LINE, so a raise mid-period is a fact about a day at one end and a fact about a window at the other, and neither shape can express the other without losing the split. (3) `PayComponentKind.overtime` is in `EARNING_KINDS` and `draftPayslip` emits exactly one earning line, always `basicPay`; `overtime` is reachable only through `arrears.ts`, which is a CORRECTION to a previous period — so a timesheet that HAD overtime lines would have nowhere to put them. The record's own observation (*an enum value nothing in the application produces*) measured from the other side, and the timesheet builder cannot produce one either, because overtime is a rule about a WEEK and no row in either schema holds one. (4) `employeeId: number` against a uuid. **The loop is therefore not closable at this joint**, and the reason is a modelling one rather than a bug: `example` prices a CONTRACT and a workforce product establishes a MEASUREMENT, and the only bridge available re-derives the contract from the measurement and then pays the contract. Whether the fix is a third basis (`measured`, whose lines ARE the gross), or a `Payslip` that can be drafted from lines rather than from a window, is the open question. Nothing here is a defect in what `example` ships — it is the input shape being the one thing that was taken on faith · [employment.ts § annualGross](example/api/src/domain/payroll/employment.ts) · [payslip.ts § draftPayslip](example/api/src/domain/payroll/payslip.ts) · [handoff.ts](../fjs-prototypes/connectteam/api/src/domain/payroll/handoff.ts) · [hours.test.ts](../fjs-prototypes/connectteam/api/test/hours.test.ts) · blocked by `FJS-D1344` |

It is why the expected list RUNS rather than skips. **One honest limit**: it grades the vitest suite, so a construct the browser drives cover reads as a survivor here; the four named ones are exactly that case. **And a trap for a CI caller** — piping it discards its exit code, which is how the first full run reported 0 with seven unexpected survivors. | <a id="fjs-1234"></a>FJS-1234 | litestone · caravan | **A predicate that depends on a ZONE held in a column cannot be a `where`, so deferred work over per-row wall-clock times is a full scan of the window: every candidate row is read and all but a few are discarded in application code.** | open | 2026-10-31 | Found building reminders on the calendly stressor (PLAN.md § Q9). The product rule is *08:00 on the morning of, in the INVITEE's zone* — the one people actually want, as against *24 hours before*, which is easy precisely because a duration needs no zone. **The query that should exist cannot be written.** `booking.inviteeTimeZone` is a column, so *has 08:00 passed for this row* is a calendar calculation per row against a different zone per row. `where` has no zone-aware operator and no index can serve one, so the sweep bounds what it can — `startsAt` between now and now+48h, an ordinary instant comparison — and asks the real question in JavaScript. **Measured on a small database: `considered 60, sent 2`.** The ratio is set by the horizon and the spread of zones, not by how many reminders are due, so it does not improve with scale — it is 2 sends from 60 reads today and 2 from 60,000 on a real calendar. **Re-measured at workforce scale on connectteam 2026-09-22, and the claim holds with one correction.** 4,000 published shifts over a fortnight, 600 people, 8 sites, a 48-hour horizon, a five-minute cron. ONE fire at 07:00Z — 08:00 where half the workforce is, the most productive instant of that day — **considered 566, sent 96**, discarding **264 pending + 206 tooLate** on the predicate that cannot be lowered and **0 past** on the one that can, in **773 ms**. Over a whole day the same window is re-read 288 times for the same 173 reminders the employer owes: **165,744 rows read, 173 sent — 1 send per 958 rows**, and **~180 seconds of CPU a day** to do it (24 fires measured at 621 ms each across the block holding both zones' 08:00; the read total is arithmetic on the measured per-fire figure, the sends are measured). **The correction is which of the two terms matters.** Moving the same 600 people from 2 zones (the brief's: Lisbon and the Azores, ONE hour apart) to 12 spread around the world left `considered` **identical at 566** and moved the sends only from 96 to 81 — spreading people over more zones spreads their 08:00s over the clock rather than changing how many there are. **So the cost is set by the horizon alone, and the spread is second order**: an employer with one hour of spread pays a global calendar's price. That removes the one escape a reader might infer from this row — that a geographically tight product is cheap. **And the cheap fix this row floats does not reach this case.** A `@generated` column holding the reminder instant fails here for a stronger reason than *cannot do arithmetic*: the zone is `User.timeZone`, which is **two relations** from `Shift` (`Shift → Employee → User`), and *which* morning is itself undecided between `Shift.onDate` (the day the manager typed, in the SITE's zone) and `startsAt` read in the person's — two columns the schema does not relate. Measured: the same shift is `tooLate` for a Lisbon employee and `pending` for an Azorean one, with reminder instants a DAY apart. **`tooLate` is a second consequence worth naming**, at 206 of 566 rows in one fire: a rule stated as a wall clock has shifts it can never remind at all — every shift starting before 08:00 local, which in a field workforce is the early turn. A rule stated as a duration has no such case, which is precisely why building that one would have measured nothing. · driven in connectteam `api/test/reminders.test.ts` § 1, § 6 **This is [FJS-1214](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1214)'s gap in a second place and the consequence is different enough to be its own row.** 1214 is about DECLARATION — a recurring wall-clock window cannot be spelled in `.lite`. This is about QUERY: the same absence of zone awareness means a zoned predicate cannot be pushed down, and the cost lands on background work rather than on a form. The arithmetic exists and is correct — `fromWall`/`partsIn` in toolbelt answered every DST case in `api/test/reminders.test.ts` first time, including a Tokyo booking whose reminder falls on the previous UTC date — so what is missing is not the maths but anywhere to put it that the database can see. **The cron half is not a defect and is worth stating so the row is not read as one.** `handle(…, { cron, timeZone })` binds ONE zone per schedule (measured: `registrations()` returns `timeZone: null` for an unzoned expression), which is right — a schedule is a statement about the app, not about a row. It is *because* that is right that the work has to become a sweep, and the sweep is where the missing predicate bites. **What would close it:** a zone-aware comparison litestone can lower — the same word [FJS-1214](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1214) asks for, reused in `where` — or, far cheaper and worth considering first, a `@generated` column holding the reminder instant, which fails today for the reason `Booking.endsAt` already documents in this app's schema: a generated column cannot reach across a relation or do arithmetic on one. **What is NOT a finding, measured and cleared:** caravan's dispatch door. `delay` is a duration and the `jobs` table stores `run_at`, an instant, which looked like `FJS-D143`'s category error one layer down — it is not. The conversion is exact (measured: `run_at` landed on the target instant, off by 0 ms), and a `runAt` option does not exist rather than being silently ignored, so TypeScript refuses it at the call site; reaching it needs a deliberate `as any`. The queue contributed durability, one-fire-per-cluster and retries, and none of Q9's difficulty came from it · [caravan/src/cron.ts](packages/caravan/src/cron.ts) · [FJS-1214](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1214) · [FJS-D143](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d143) · blocked by `FJS-D1108` · 2026-10-20: FJS-D908 was ruled A on 2026-10-13 (a zone-aware operator the client lowers), so that blocked by no longer holds; FJS-D1108, what exactly D908 means, is still owed and still holds the row · [FJS-D908](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d908) · Second sighting, clinical stressor (PLAN Q4), 2026-10-30, in a ROW POLICY rather than a where: a proxy grant ends the day the child turns 16 in the PATIENT's zone (Patient.timeZone, falling back to Clinic.timeZone). '@@allow(read, proxyGrants.some(...) && dateOfBirth > now() - 16yr)' compiles and is UTC; 'now(timeZone) - 16yr' is refused 'Expected RPAREN, got timeZone'. So the grant opens/closes at UTC midnight, up to a day off in America/Chicago. Seeded child born 2010-11-01 shows it: dev clock was 2026-10-30 local / 2026-10-31 UTC. · Measured, clinical measure/proxy.mjs, 2026-10-30: the policy 'dateOfBirth > now() - 16yr' follows UTC both ways. Wall clock 01:02Z (20:02 Oct 30 in Chicago): a Chicago child born 2010-10-31 is shut out (404) five hours before their local birthday. Injected now = 12:00Z: a Pacific/Kiritimati child born 2010-11-01 (16 locally since 10:00Z) still reads (true); at 01:00Z next day false -- open fourteen hours past the local birthday. |

But the interface also carries `[key: string]: unknown`, so `$.locals.brandng` is legal and answers `unknown`, where `app.brandng` is an error because `App` has no index signature. A misspelled read is silent on the surface the ruling just made the recommended one. **Not fixable by deleting the signature**: `paginate` and `db` are written by framework hooks and app code writes ad-hoc keys today, so removing it breaks every unaugmented app. Wants the shape that keeps both — a declared key typed and an undeclared one still writable — which is a different mechanism from the one `app.own()` uses. Sits against [`FJS-D199`](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d199), which rules that junction refuses an unknown AUTHORING key by name; a locals key is per-call state rather than authoring, so the two are not in conflict, but they are the same question asked of two surfaces and they answer differently | open | 2026-09-04 | [context.ts `ServiceContextLocals`](packages/junction/src/core/context.ts) · [`FJS-706`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-706) · `FJS-D200` · Invariant 5 · seam: `$` · blocked by `FJS-D1349` |

## Needs a decision

These are questions, not defects. A ruling moves to `DECISIONS.md` and closes the
row here. **This table is the questions with an id; most open questions are argued
inside an IDEAS paper's `## Open questions` and stay there.** `fli decisions` reads
both as one queue, and a question becomes pickable — by `fli decide` or on `fli gui`
— once its bullet carries lettered options and a `**Recommend X**` line. A row's
cell cannot hold options, so they go in the paper its Detail links.

Options: (A) clearing the file leaves an @immutable sibling alone — the digest becomes a record of what WAS held, the pair's invariant 'sha256 is the hash of file' holding only while file is set; (B) a second argument, `@digest(sha256, keep)`, says so per column; (C) no change — the app keeps a second plain column for the never-twice index and lets @digest own the first. | <a id="fjs-d1131"></a>FJS-D1131 | litestone · junction | **Is a foreign wire format (Bitwarden's Type: 2, RevisionDate, Object: "cipher" — names and values fixed by a client somebody else wrote) the plugin's alone, or may the schema point at it — @map renames the column and nothing a caller touches, @label is a human title, an enum member carries no value** | [IDEAS/owed-rulings.md](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) · vaultwarden Q1's pre-run guess is 'a ruling, not a word' · [open-questions.md § Cannot say C8](../fjs-prototypes/vaultwarden/discovery/open-questions.md) · Measured, vaultwarden Phase 1 (bw 2026.10.0 logging in with TOTP against the real app, measure/bw-login.mjs green). The client asked for exactly nine things to log in, sync and list: POST /identity/accounts/prelogin/password, POST /identity/connect/token (form-urlencoded; grant_type password with twoFactorToken/Provider/Remember in the SAME request when a code is given, and refresh_token), GET /api/config, GET /api/sync, GET /api/accounts/revision-date, POST /api/accounts/key-management/user-key-id, plus the legacy prelogin paths. All nine are raw routes in one app plugin (api/src/bitwarden/plugin.ts); no service was touched and the model names never reach the wire. Four things the framework had to be worked around on: (1) the access token must be a JWT the client decodes (sub, email, sstamp, exp), and Junction resolves every Bearer through auth.verifySession, so an Object.create(auth) wrapper unwraps a sid claim — six lines, verifySession IS the seam, cleared; (2) the OAuth error JSON (invalid_grant + error_description, 400) is translated by the plugin in a try/catch around auth.login, a second thrown-value→HTTP translator beside toResponse (Invariant 4) with no per-route hook to hand the owner a dialect; (3) /identity/* sits outside apiPrefix and so on app.http.router, which drops the request scope (FJS-3104); (4) Junction serves no TLS and the client refuses http (FJS-3105). The pre-run guess holds as far as it goes — an app plugin over raw routes — and the ruling should say what the framework owes it: the request scope on every route it registers, and a way for a plugin to own the error translation for ITS routes; the schema points at nothing (Type: 2, RevisionDate stay the plugin's). |

| <a id="fjs-3991"></a>FJS-3991 | litestone — **A create or update refused after its file is stored -- by SQLite (a taken id, a unique, a check) or by a later field's serialize -- keeps the object and nothing removes it; a refused update also leaves its stashed old ref queued for the next update's cleanup** | 2026-11-04 | ExternalRefPlugin stored in its before hooks and cleaned only in onAfterWrite, which a refused write never reaches, and it queued the replaced ref in one per-flavor slot, so the next update of that model deleted the file the row still held. Fixed by FJS-D1873: a new Observer, onWriteSettled(model, operation, args, error, ctx), fired once per create/createMany/update/updateMany/upsertMany call by settlingWrites (client.js), and tx.hold({ commit, rollback }) (transaction.js), held to the outermost commit and fired on its frame's rollback, which exclusive() awaits. ExternalRefPlugin keys what a write stored and replaced on args.data (_serializeField, _replaces): refused, it deletes what it stored and hands the caller's payload back; landed, it holds the old-ref cleanup to commit and the new objects' deletion to rollback. onAfterDelete is held the same way. The flavor stash and FileStorage's _followOrDrop are gone. test/file-from-stream.test.ts § FJS-3991: a taken id, a later field's @accept, a unique on update, and a $transaction rolling back a create, an update and a delete (red before: 2, 4 and 5 objects, and the row's file deleted); litestone 8117 pass (one README fence flaked under load, 85/85 alone), junction 3509, sierra test:safety 12/12, immich unique-after-store leftUnderRoot 0. · [external-ref.js](packages/litestone/src/plugins/external-ref.js) · [transaction.js](packages/litestone/src/core/transaction.js) |
| <a id="fjs-3985"></a>FJS-3985 | litestone — **A create whose stated @digest sibling disagrees with the bytes is refused AFTER the object is stored, and nothing removes it: an orphaned file per refused create, on File, fromStream, fromPath and fromPath move alike** | 2026-11-04 | The objects were stored by serialize before _followBytes compared the stated @digest sibling, and a write that throws reaches no onAfterWrite, so nothing deleted them; on an update the old ref stashed for cleanup also stayed queued, and the next update of that model on the same client deleted the file the row still held. FileStoragePlugin now notes each File value a write hands bytes to before serialize (_written) and, when _followBytes refuses, deletes every object that write stored -- File[] items on the same row included -- and on an update forgets the stash it queued (_followOrDrop, file-storage.js). A moved fromPath source is not put back: its bytes disagree with their claim. test/file-from-stream.test.ts: a refused sibling leaves no object for bytes, File, fromStream, fromPath and fromPath move, and a refused update leaves the row's file standing through the next write (red before; the stash half goes red alone with its line stubbed). |

| <a id="fjs-d1815"></a>FJS-D1815 | cli · desktop — **How does a wrapped desktop app whose API reads the person's local drives (immich Q7, ruled A) run that API on the person's machine — a sidecar the shell starts and supervises, the API bundled into the shell, or the person runs it — and which plugins does make:desktop declare for it: dialog (pick a folder), fs scope, autostart and tray (keep reading while the window is closed)?** | 2026-11-04 | Ruled [`FJS-D1815`](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d1815): **A** — this paper's launcher as a Tauri sidecar: packages compiled in, bun inside (Q5 A), the app's own files shipped as resources beside it (Q1 A), data in the OS app-data directory (Q4 B; `%APPDATA%\<identifier>` on Windows). The shell starts it on a free `127.0.0.1` port, hands the page that origin, restarts it when it dies and stops it on Quit. Closing the window hides it to a tray (Open, Quit) and autostart at login is an opt-in; the shell declares the dialog, tray and autostart plugins, and not fs, because the API reads the drives, not the page. Cost: a bun binary per target triple (`bun build --compile --target bun-windows-x64`, …), a port the bundle cannot know at build time, and walls 1–6 met again on Windows, where nothing has run. · [desktop-surface.js](packages/cli/core/desktop-surface.js) · [PLAN.md](../fjs-prototypes/immich/PLAN.md) |

| <a id="fjs-3926"></a>FJS-3926 | mesa — **A bare undefined identifier at module level in a .mesa (const resource = groups, where the export is matchGroups) passes fli check's mesa-compiles and vite build with no warning, and at runtime the whole layout is blank — no nav, an empty #app — with only a console.error to say why** | 2026-11-04 | Cause: the compiler never read a <script module> for names it does not declare, so a rename that left const resource = groups behind compiled clean, vite build tree-shook it to a bare "groups," statement, and the route module threw a ReferenceError at import — a blank layout with one console line. Proof: two cases in test/compile-errors.test.js (the first goes red with the call stubbed), the mesa vitest suite 2590 green, and 120 real script-module files in example/ and packages/ compile with no false refusal. | <a id="fjs-3509"></a>FJS-3509 | basecamp — **edge.test.ts's sweep row saw the ingress A record hold only 203.0.113.5 after online1 went quiet** | 2026-11-01 | Cause: a torn read in the test, not the zone. The Cloudflare sink pages two records at a time (PAGE_CAP, so the connector's walk is exercised) and slices by offset, and zone-shop spans pages; when the lose(online1) push's delete of .5 landed between two of ingressAt's page GETs, the slice shifted and .6 was skipped, so the poll read ['203.0.113.5'] — a set the zone never held — and until(length === 1) took it. Probed against the real sink: layout [mx, www, cname, .5, .6], a delete of .5 after page 2 gives a walk of [.5] while the zone is [.6]. The other waits are safe: drain deletes the last record and undrain and check-in append, so nothing shifts. Fix: the wait is on the value the push should leave (v.join() === '203.0.113.6'), so a torn read polls again; the status-naming throw stays for a real miss. | <a id="fjs-1078"></a>FJS-1078 | cli — **`serviceForModel` hand-rolls Invariant 2's model name and disagrees with the owner on 7 of 12 real service names — in a function one command calls.** [`FJS-975`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-975) closed 2026-09-07 by giving `@frontierjs/toolbelt/inflect` the shape half and consolidating six copies, and it names `split(/[-_]/)` in the cli as one of them. `core/app-schema.js:302` is a survivor it did not reach, with a regex that handles no separator at all: `addresses` → `Addres`, `people` → `People`, and `journal-entries` → `Journal-entry`, which is the exact `Order-item` failure that row describes — not an identifier. `modelName` answers `Address`, `Person`, `JournalEntry`. **Two facts keep it at S4 and both belong in the row**: one command calls it, `fli admin:generate` (`commands/admin/generate.md:453`), which is corrected 2026-09-13 from *nothing calls it* — a grep over `.js` alone misses a command written as markdown, and every hyphenated service in `example` states `model:` explicitly — `product-variants.service.ts` carries a comment saying it is STATED rather than derived — so no app here reaches the wrong answer today, and `admin:generate` over a hyphenated service without `model:` would. That is also what makes it worth filing rather than fixing in passing: a latent copy of a consolidated fact is how the consolidation comes undone, and the next caller inherits it silently. The fix is one line pointing at `modelName`, since deleting it would break `admin:generate`. | 2026-11-01 | Cause: serviceForModel spelled the model name with a hand-rolled regex chain (addresses → Addres, journal-entries → Journal-entry). Note the row's claim that people → Person was wrong: the owner leaves irregulars alone (inflect.js header), so it answers People, as the hand copy did. | <a id="fjs-d1705"></a>FJS-D1705 | litestone — **May a create name a parent the caller cannot read when the row being written is what opens that parent's read policy?** | 2026-11-01 | Ruled [`FJS-D1705`](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d1705): **A** — grade after the write: for a hidden parent, insert inside the write's unit, re-ask the parent's `exists()` under the caller, and roll back with the identical 422 if it is still hidden. | <a id="fjs-629"></a>FJS-629 | example · junction — **There is no way to remove a person.** **The gap this row was filed for has closed** — a `methods: [{ method, gate }]` entry grades a custom method now (`customMethodGrade`, [`FJS-1087`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-1087)), which is the third candidate below — so what is left is `example`'s `users.remove` itself, still unbuilt, and `verify:users` still leaving an account behind. As filed: `example`'s `users` service declines DELETE deliberately — auth keeps `Credential` and `Session` at `@@gate("8")` with `userId` as a bare String and no relation behind it, so removing a `User` through the ORM leaves live sessions authenticating against a row that is gone. The correct operation is `IAuth.deleteUser(id)`, which clears credentials, sessions and the address's pending verification tokens and then removes the row — and it cannot be reached from a service without becoming a CUSTOM method, which is where the gap is. **`gateAuth` grades CRUD against the model's `@@gate` and says nothing about a custom method** — junction states it in the source: *a method the map does not name is not gated here*. So `users.remove` would have to establish its own authority, and the only tools available are `if (level < 5)`, which is the seed's rule written a second time in a place nothing keeps in step (the mistake `payments.refund` documents at length and refuses to make), or a hand-rolled hook. `payments.refund`'s own answer does not generalize: it asks `db.order.transitions(row)`, which works because a refund IS a declared move, and removing a person is not one. **The near miss is what makes it worth filing.** `@@gate` is single-valued, so an `extend model` may not restate it — which is why `create` had to be expressed as `@@allow('create', auth().isAdmin)` instead, and that worked precisely because create is a CRUD operation the gate map names. There is no counterpart for a method the app invents. Three candidate shapes and they are different features: a per-method gate in the seed (`methods { remove @gate(5) }`), extending `@@capabilities` to cover a non-move custom method (`FJS-D149` ruled that a non-CRUD action earns a capability *by being a move* — this is the case that is not), or a declared `gate:` on the `methods:` entry beside `input:`, which is the cheapest and keeps the declaration in the service where the method is. **The cost while it is open is measurable**: `verify:users` leaves one account behind on every run and cannot sweep it, so every count in that drive is a delta or a re-read rather than an absolute | 2026-10-11 | Already built, in the wrong place: @frontierjs/auth's `people` service ships `remove` at declared gate 5 (it calls `IAuth.deleteUser`, clearing credentials, sessions and pending tokens) and example mounts it, so no per-method gate on `users` was needed — the `methods: [{ method, gate }]` form of FJS-1087 is what grades it. What was left was the drive: `verify:users` now sweeps its own accounts through DELETE /people/:id (shopper 403, admin 200, a removed person's session 401) and first sweeps earlier runs' `<letter>-<6>@shop.test` leftovers, which had piled to 132 rows and pushed the seeded people past the drive's $limit=100 read. Stubbing the door to /users reds four checks; 105/105 on private ports. users.service.ts and the drive header now point at people.remove. · [users.service.ts](example/api/src/services/users.service.ts) · [litestone.ts `gateAuth`](packages/junction/src/core/litestone.ts) · [payments.service.ts](example/api/src/services/payments.service.ts) · [FJS-D149](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d149) |

| <a id="fjs-914"></a>FJS-914 | litestone — **Validation runs ahead of the gate, so a caller the gate refuses still learns a model's column names.** The `@guarded` half is FIXED (2026-09-05) and this row is what is left. As filed: `sortableKeysFor`/`filterableKeysFor` walked every field and excluded relation, `@computed`, `@transient`, `@edge`/`@scoped` and opaque types and nothing else, and the set reached a caller in both message branches — the list (`Sortable: …` / `Valid fields: …`) and one name at a time through `suggestKey`, which is the branch a real typo takes. Measured as `$setAuth(null)` reading ``Sortable: createdAt, email, id, notes, ssn`` off a model gated `@@gate("1.1.5.9")` that refused the same caller a legitimate read one line later. **What was done**: `_guardedNames`/`_shownSet` narrow what a refusal DISCLOSES at four sites — `checkOrderBy`, `checkWhereKeys` and both bridges (`$checkWhere`, `$checkOrderBy`, which junction's `autoFilter` answers a 400 from). Legality is untouched **deliberately**: `$checkWhere` states that validity is a question about the schema and every flavor must answer it identically, so filtering the legal set would make one caller's standing decide another's 400. The two bridges are called outside any call in progress, where `ctx.isSystem` has nothing to answer with, so they narrow for EVERY caller — the safe direction, and right, since a boundary's caller is never the system context. `test/guarded-disclosure.test.ts`, 5 tests, **3 red with `_shownSet` stubbed to identity**; suite 4334 pass / 0 fail. **What remains, and why the row stays open**: a below-gate caller still learns the ORDINARY column names, because validation runs before the gate — S3 now rather than S2, since what crosses is no longer a column `FJS-D205` rules out. Fixing it means moving the gate ahead of arg validation, which is unsized: `AccessDeniedError` is raised from several places and the reorder changes what a legitimate developer with a typo sees. **Not a defect and left alone**: naming a `@guarded` column EXACTLY is still refused in its own sentence, which already argues the inference channel — *ordering by it leaks the ordering of every row at once* | 2026-10-11 | Cause: key validation (`guardArgs`) ran before `GatePlugin`, so a caller the gate refuses read the model's ordinary column names in `Sortable:` / `Valid fields:` / `Did you mean`. Fix at the owner: `GatePlugin.onInit` publishes `ctx.gateCheck`, and `withArgValidation` answers a `ValidationError` with the gate's refusal first (read, create, update, delete by verb, `search` and `create` included). Only the failure path pays, and a caller the gate admits still hears the typo. `test/guarded-disclosure.test.ts` +8 tests (7 red with the check stubbed); `elegance-fixes` combinator test moved to `updateMany` since VERIFIED is below Lead's delete gate; litestone suite 6891 pass / 0 fail · [client.js `_shownSet`](packages/litestone/src/core/client.js) · [test/guarded-disclosure.test.ts](packages/litestone/test/guarded-disclosure.test.ts) · [FJS-D205](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d205) · [FJS-553](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-553) · [FJS-554](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-554) |

| <a id="fjs-2318"></a>FJS-2318 | litestone · sierra — **The browser worker bundles the whole .lite parser and never parses — about 30% of the worker on every page load** | 2026-10-10 | The parser is out of the worker's load path. pointColumns/pointColumnNames moved to ddl.js and inferFromFk to schema-maps.js, which also breaks three import cycles. createClient imports parser.js lazily, only when there is text or a path to parse. A split bundle of the worker loads 473 KB instead of 657 KB (164 KB vs 210 KB gzip). Vite builds a worker as an IIFE, which inlines a lazy import, so Sierra builds the worker with its own plugin list: localDbWorkerPlugins (build/local-db-plugin.js) resolves litestone's public ./parser export and swaps in a stub that throws by name. An ES worker without the stub was measured and rejected: it grew the shell by 9 kB and still precached the parser. So was a `#parser` package condition in litestone with a stub under a custom condition: Vite 8 honors it in an IIFE worker, but a worker plugin can set it only by mutating an array the page config shares, and a top-level condition stubs the page as well. | <a id="fjs-266"></a>FJS-266 | repo — **The framework tells an app to run Biome and runs nothing itself.** `FJS-D32` adopted a linter and `@frontierjs/config` ships the rule set every scaffolded app extends, but this repo does not extend it — a framework that lints itself with nothing while telling its users to lint has two answers to one question, which is the shape Invariant 4 exists to prevent. It was not turned on because the number was measured first: Biome's `recommended` gives **7,249** findings on this tree, and the shipped curated set gives **~600**, of which 123 are `noUnusedImports` and 25 are `noGlobalIsNan`. That is a countable cleanup with a direction, not the taste argument `IDEAS/tooling-decisions.md` 1 was blocked on. Work: add the devDependency and a root `biome.json` extending the package, clear the findings, then add a `lint` phase to `scripts/ci.mjs` — in that order, since a phase added first is a phase everyone learns to skip. One unexplained finding to resolve on the way: **Biome cannot parse `packages/mesa/test/runtime.test.js`** | 2026-10-10 | The repo now lints itself: @biomejs/biome 2.5.8 is a root devDependency and a root biome.json extends @frontierjs/config (whose own biome.json became root:false, or Biome refuses two roots), excluding only what is vendored or specification (vendor, mockup, .jetty-cache, html, svelte). The measured number had drifted — 4,218 findings, 2,740 of them vendored bundles — and was cleared to zero by autofix (unused imports and variables, parseInt radix, hasOwn, Number.isNaN where the operand was already a number), hand edits (void returns, a catch parameter assigned, a duplicate key, dead private field) and 53 biome-ignore comments each carrying its reason. The shipped set gained four principled loosenings with README reasons: useIterableCallbackReturn skips forEach, noEmptyInterface and noImplicitAnyLet off, folder patterns without the trailing /** (peer range now >=2.2.0). The unexplained parse finding was a duplicate $$eachBlock import in mesa/test/runtime.test.js (and a stray CSS fragment in mesa/example/index.html). scripts/ci.mjs has a lint phase (biome lint --error-on-warnings, 2.6s, fast tier) that passes. Proved by the suites of config, toolbelt, css, mesa, sierra, junction, litestone, caravan, auth, conduit, mcp, orion, outpost, jetty, email-kit, ui, basecamp and vscode, and the example verify:offline/widget/jobs/cart/pay drives; autofix broke css's page-injected scripts and two sierra destructures, caught by those suites and reverted. · [packages/config/biome.json](packages/config/biome.json) · [IDEAS/tooling-decisions.md](IDEAS/tooling-decisions.md) |

| <a id="fjs-940"></a>FJS-940 | junction — **A key inside a `junction.config.js` section is still stashed and read by nothing, and the interfaces cannot be the list that would catch it.** [`FJS-939`](ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md#fjs-939) closed the TOP-LEVEL half — a section nothing reads is refused by name at `start()`. So a nested check means hand-keeping a key list per section beside an interface nobody updates, which is the second origin `FJS-D199` exists to remove. **What would make it decidable is one owner per section for *what keys does this have***, read by the reader AND the check the way `JUNCTION_SECTIONS` now is — six sections, so six lists, and the subsystem that consumes each one is the only honest place for it. **Measured 2026-09-13**: [`FJS-D256`](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d256) gave `middleware:` and `plugins:` that owner for what the FRAMEWORK declares — `loadConfig` maps each key one at a time and `test/config-surface.test.ts` grades both directions — but a caller's misspelled key in any section is still dropped in silence, which is this row | 2026-10-10 | A key inside a `junction.config.js` section was merged in silence because no list of a section's keys existed that the reader and the check shared. | <a id="fjs-2317"></a>FJS-2317 | litestone — **@@trail added 100–170 µs to every audited write, twenty times the create it records, because each entry paid its own index commit** | 2026-10-10 | Found by the 2026-10-09 performance audit (R5), whose diagnosis was half right. Split on this machine: building the entry is ~3 µs, the bare JSONL append ~14 µs, and the index's BEGIN IMMEDIATE + INSERT + COMMIT ~90–120 µs — five B-tree pages (the table and four indexes) into the WAL per line, plus the checkpoints they bring. The create pipeline the audit blamed is not the cost, so no raw append path was built. Fix: fireLog queues per log table, and the entries one tick produced go down as one createMany, so one lock and one commit; a lone write is still one create. A batch that throws is retried entry by entry, so one entry a SQL trail's own model refuses drops that entry and not the others, and $logStats counts per entry. A SQL trail's batch announces one collection event where single creates announced rows. Ablation create/log-audit: +168 µs to +25 µs at load ~10. That bench writes in one tick, so the gain is for a request or job writing several rows; a request writing one row still pays one commit. Proved by trail-batch.test.ts (one createMany per tick, lines in order with the index naming each, the refused-entry fallback); log-flush-on-exit.test.ts unchanged · [audit-log.js](packages/litestone/src/core/audit-log.js) · [trail-batch.test.ts](packages/litestone/test/trail-batch.test.ts) |

| <a id="fjs-2314"></a>FJS-2314 | litestone · sierra — **The OPFS pool VFS refuses `journal_mode = WAL` in silence, so every autocommit write on a device was a rollback-journal cycle: 10–12 ms a row in Chrome** | 2026-10-09 | Found by the 2026-10-09 performance audit (B1). The pool has no xShmMap, so the WAL pragma answers the previous mode and `synchronous = NORMAL` did nothing. Measured in Chrome over the pool, 300 autocommit inserts: DELETE/NORMAL 12.1 ms, PERSIST/NORMAL 6.3, PERSIST/OFF 0.113, MEMORY/OFF 0.063. Fix: an engine may declare `journal: { mode, synchronous }` (checked against SQLite's words in setEngine, since it is spliced into a PRAGMA); sqlite-wasm declares PERSIST/OFF, which keeps a journal that rolls back a killed tab — MEMORY would lose the file to one. Only a power loss mid-commit can cost the file, which is a cache (unsent writes live in IndexedDB). The wasm path no longer reaches applyWal, so its SharedArrayBuffer busy-retry cannot fire in a worker. Proved by the browser drive (new row: 30 single creates under 2.5 ms each, red at 10.1) and engine-seam.test.ts (a bad journal refused by name). · [sqlite-wasm.js](packages/litestone/src/engines/sqlite-wasm.js) · [databases.js](packages/litestone/src/core/databases.js) · [engine.js](packages/litestone/src/core/engine.js) |
| <a id="fjs-2313"></a>FJS-2313 | litestone — **Every non-system write ran one exists() per foreign key it named, whether or not the parent could hide anything, so a plain create naming two parents was three statements** | 2026-10-09 | Found by the 2026-10-09 performance audit (R2). A gate refusal falls through to the existing two-query verdict. The audit's proposed skip list left out soft delete, templates and the effective window, which would have admitted a create under a soft-deleted parent; deriving from READ_RULES cannot drift that way. Proved by fast-paths.test.ts (no exists() for an open parent; red on HEAD) and hidden-parent.test.ts unchanged. · [client.js](packages/litestone/src/core/client.js) |
| <a id="fjs-2312"></a>FJS-2312 | litestone — **One @@gate or @@allow anywhere in a schema turned the findUnique-by-pk and findMany({}) fast paths off for every model, and every verb scanned every model's shape for a policied aggregate** | 2026-10-09 | Found by the 2026-10-09 performance audit (R3, R4). Both preconditions were client-wide (`ctx.hasPolicies`, `plugins.hasPlugins`), so in basecamp — every model gated — the paths were dead code. Fix: each READ_RULES row declares `narrows` (refused at load without one), and the fast paths run when no rule but soft delete narrows this model for this flavor, with the plugin beforeRead/afterRead hooks around the statement; a beforeRead that rewrites the args is honored by asking the shape again after it. buildSQL's own shortcut, which assumed the old preconditions, asks the same and only for a read verb. The aggregate scan is `ctx.hasPoliciedAggregates`, computed once. Measured A/B in a gated app: findUnique 3.7 µs against 5.3–6.7 on HEAD (load ~8). Proved by fast-paths.test.ts (path taken in a gated app, red on HEAD; gate refusal, afterRead, a plugin read filter, a rewriting beforeRead), verbs-rules and litestone suites, basecamp verify 349/349 in an isolated worktree. · [client.js](packages/litestone/src/core/client.js) · [args.js](packages/litestone/src/core/args.js) |
| <a id="fjs-2311"></a>FJS-2311 | litestone — **tenants.create() with no migrations directory ran every DDL statement autocommit: 3.6–4.0 s per tenant on a 188-model schema, and a statement that threw left a half-built file behind** | 2026-10-09 | Found by the 2026-10-09 performance audit (P1, P2). | <a id="fjs-2310"></a>FJS-2310 | litestone · sierra — **A device never ran a migration, so a @@sync model gaining a column kept its old table and every write-through naming the column failed: the device held nothing and said so only offline** | 2026-10-09 | Found by the 2026-10-09 performance audit (side finding), reproduced in Chrome: `table shelf has no column named aisle`. Fix: the worker marks the file with a hash of the DDL its schema generates, in PRAGMA user_version (readable before a client exists, no table for introspection to find), and discards a built file whose mark differs before createClient opens it — a device holds a window of the server's rows and its unsent writes live in IndexedDB (sierra pending.js), so it is refilled, not migrated. | <a id="fjs-2296"></a>FJS-2296 | litestone — **A findMany `window` spec puts every column name into the SQL verbatim, so a scoped caller reads a @guarded column through `window: { p: { max: "pin" } }` and a crafted name runs any subquery; an unknown name answers 0 or null instead of being refused** | 2026-10-10 | The window builder spliced every name, number and keyword of a window spec into the pattern, and the client never asked whether a name was a column the caller may aggregate, so a scoped caller read a @guarded column through max, a quote in a lag name closed the identifier and appended a subquery, and an unknown name answered a constant. findMany now holds every name windowColumnNames lists to refuseAggregateKeys — function arguments at the value tier, partitionBy and orderBy at the naming tier — and buildWindowCols quotes each through quoteIdent under the model's columnMap, takes offset, n, ntile and frame bounds only as integers, direction and nulls only as their keywords, and a default only as a primitive. test/window-names.test.ts (five red before the fix, seven green after, incl. an @map case); the sql-idents ceiling for query.js lowered 75 to 62. · [query.js](packages/litestone/src/core/query.js#L2431) · [args.js](packages/litestone/src/core/args.js#L695) |
| <a id="fjs-2062"></a>FJS-2062 | litestone · mcp · junction — **A caller over JSON or /mcp cannot supply a File column at all: the tool schema asks for the stored reference object and the ORM refuses every object for a File column, so an app whose core flow is an upload cannot do that flow through its own agent** | 2026-10-10 | Per FJS-D666 (A): FileStorage reads a base64 data URL or { name, type, data } as bytes (readValue → readInline; non-base64 refused by name, @accept grades the sniffed bytes), and generateJsonSchema's create/update modes point a File column and a File[]'s items at a new FileInput def instead of the stored FileRef, so the /mcp create tool describes the bytes. | <a id="fjs-d666"></a>FJS-D666 | litestone — **How does a JSON or /mcp caller supply a File column: an inline data-URL value FileStorage reads as bytes, an upload route whose ref the create then accepts, or both?** | 2026-10-10 | Ruled [`FJS-D666`](DECISIONS.md#fjs-d666): **A** — an inline value: a data URL (RFC 2397, `data:<mime>;base64,…`) or `{ name, type, data }` with base64 `data`, which `readValue` decodes into bytes like a Buffer, `@accept` sniffing the bytes and not trusting the claimed type. The input schema for a File column is derived to describe that value rather than `FileRef`. The bound is junction's `http.maxBodySize`, the one a browser's multipart upload already meets, so it is not a new option. Its default is 256KB and base64 adds a third, so about 190KB of file gets through untouched: a phone photo (2–5MB) is refused until the app raises that setting, which is the same raise a form upload of that photo already needs. Today the 413 reads *Request body exceeds 262144 bytes* and names nothing to raise, so it names `http.maxBodySize`. One call, and the server stays the only author of a ref. · [IDEAS/owed-rulings.md](IDEAS/owed-rulings.md) |
